newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes seen firm; Tapis done at $1.70/bbl.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes seen firm; Tapis done at $1.70/bbl.

text.p: Cash crude prices in Asia were firm on Wednesday as trading gradually shifted to next-month trading.
A producer sold a cargo of February Tapis to a Thai refiner at a premium of $1.70 per barrel -- 10 cents higher than the last deal over Christmas.
The producer said it had just one cargo of Tapis left in February, for lifting after February 20. However, the producer has tended to bring forward barrels in the past.
But with some Australian fields down because of Cyclone Rachel, the light sweet market was well underpinned.

The 90,000 bpd Cossack and 70,000 bpd Griffin fields -- the biggest affected by the cyclone -- hoped to come back up in the next 48 hours, but shipping delays were 7-10 days, traders said. Balance January Tapis paper was traded at $25.70 per barrel between a bank and a major, 10 cents higher than day-earlier assessments. February paper was assessed at $25.30/$25.60, implying an outright price of $27.00 plus.

Oman crude was heard possibly traded into China as high as MPM +31 cents -- although the deal could not be confirmed and there was some confusion as to whether it was a late trading February or a March deal.
If March, it would effectively add 18 cents to premiums. February premiums went out around 30 cents, but the Dubai-Oman spread for March widened 18 cents.
Traders said several Asian crudes were underpinned by China demand. The February Minas premium was talked at plus $1.00 after January went out around plus 87 cents.
China bid higher than MPM plus 20 cents for March Oman in recent days. It has since cut back its bid to 15 to 20 cents, traders said.
China was heard buying as many as four VLCCs of West African grades in the past week for January loading.
